title: Linux.Mirai_Incident_Response_248
description: Investigate and respond to a Linux.Mirai trojan incident on a victim host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has exhibited unusual behavior, including unexpected outbound network connections and elevated CPU usage. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential security incident involving the Linux.Mirai trojan.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the victim host for unauthorized or suspicious services that may indicate trojan activity.
levels.solution: Check running services and their associated processes for anything unusual or unexpected. The service name associated with the trojan's persistence mechanism is `network-diagnostics.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and their associated processes for anything unusual or unexpected.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system applications.

levels.title: Investigate Scheduled Tasks
levels.content: Determine if any scheduled tasks or timers are responsible for automatically executing the malware on the victim host.
levels.solution: Investigate systemd timers and services that may be triggering malicious activity. The name of the timer or task responsible for the trojan's scheduled execution is `network-diagnostics.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers and services that may be triggering malicious activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that are not part of the standard system applications.

levels.title: Locate Malware Files
levels.content: Locate files installed by the malware on the victim host that may provide further evidence of the compromise.
levels.solution: Search for hidden or unusual directories and files that do not belong to standard system applications. The filename of a key component used by the trojan for its malicious activities is `/usr/local/lib/.netd/revshell.sh`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Search for hidden or unusual directories and files that do not belong to standard system applications.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for files in directories like `/usr/local/lib/.netd`.
